title: add-actor-rag-playground-tool-scheduler-and-plugin-scaffold
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: Provide a compact, reproducible developer quickstart that demonstrates stateful RAG workflows using an actor-style runtime. Many existing quickstarts show single-turn retrieval+generation or tool-calling; this PR introduces a lightweight 'Actor Playground' where developers can compose long-lived session actors that manage tool scheduling, deterministic step ordering, and checkpointed RAG state.

Summary of changes: Adds an examples/actor-playground workspace with a TypeScript runtime shim, a minimal Rust-based session actor (WASM-optional), an authoring web UI for wiring tools to actor tasks, and a plugin scaffold that makes it straightforward to add connectors (vector DBs, file stores, third-party APIs). Includes a step-by-step quickstart in README.md, a migration guide for teams moving from single-call RAG scripts to session actors, runner configs for local dev and containerized deployment, and telemetry hooks for Redwood Console.

Why this is different: The actor model emphasizes explicit task boundaries (fetch, score, synthesize, store) and a deterministic scheduler so teams can reason about regression tests, replay sessions, and checkpoint-based cost estimation. This playground demonstrates both synchronous and streaming modes, and includes a simple fallback policy that shows how to swap to a smaller model variant during high load while preserving actor state.

What reviewers should focus on: correctness of the actor scheduling contract, clarity of the quickstart and migration guide, safety of the plugin scaffold API surface (no secrets in example plugins), and observability integration points.

How to run (short): 1) cd examples/actor-playground 2) yarn install && yarn dev (starts authoring UI + local runtime) 3) node ./ts/playground-runner.js --example=multi-turn-session 4) open http://localhost:3000 to step through the actor graph. Full instructions and Docker compose included in README.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart end-to-end demo - [x] TS runtime + example actors - [x] Plugin scaffold for connectors - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] CI test coverage for scheduler invariants - [x] Telemetry hooks wired

Related: references ENG-4821 (actor scheduler research), PM-331 (product requirements for session persistence).
